text:
maria: ran a 2h profile on canary with the new continuous-batcher changes. saw a weird kernel flip when mixed decode-rate requests are in the same batch. p95 jumped ~20% during peak mix. attaching short summary below.

ashok: ugh. flip as in we picked slower kernel for whole batch? can you paste the sample trace?

maria: yep. snippet from trace:
```
batch_id=0x7f3e kernel_selected=fast_matmul
batch_id=0x7f3e -> merged with batch 0x7fa1 (decode_rate mismatch)
kernel_selected=slow_attention (fallback)
latency_p95 +180ms
```

maria: also saw KV cache hit rate drop from 0.82 -> 0.69 for those interleaved batches, likely because prefetching didn't align with the new batch shape.

perf-bot: perf summary (canary): throughput 128 req/s -> 123 req/s, p50 78ms, p95 472ms -> 564ms spike windows, KV hit 82% -> 69% on mixed workload windows.

zane: my hunch: batch formation currently prioritizes queue time and overall token budget only. it doesn't enforce decode-rate strata. when a slow-decoder request joins a fast group, kernel selector sees longer expected tail and picks the robust kernel. that regresses the fast requests.

taylor: agreed. we tried enforcing length buckets before, but decode-rate is different signal. can we classify requests into short/long decode-rate buckets at admission and prefer homogeneous batches? maybe do soft affinity rather than hard partition to avoid starvation.

maria: experiment plan: 1) add decode_rate_estimate tag at admission (tokens/sec based on model+prompt_length) 2) maintain 3 strata: <200 t/s, 200-800 t/s, >800 t/s 3) when forming batch prefer same-strata peers up to token_budget but allow cross-strata if waiting >50ms 4) update kernel selection heuristics to consider decode_rate_percentile of batch.

ashok: for step 1 how do we compute estimate cheaply? we can use historical mean decode_rate per route+model plus a small scaling factor for length. e.g., estimate = lookup(route,model).mean * (prompt_tokens/typical_prompt). cheap and cacheable.

zane: implementation note: keep strata as small ints on request metadata so it travels through queue and multiplexer. this avoids adding heavy objects to hot path.

perf-bot: rolled canary patch to 10% traffic with strata-based batching. initial 30m snapshot: p95 down from 564ms-> 416ms on mixed workload windows, KV hit improved 69%->80%, throughput steady. no allocation spikes.

maria: nice. also observed fewer kernel flips: kernel_consistency metric went from 0.62 -> 0.87. will run longer stability run tonight.

ashok: next: tune the wait threshold. 50ms seems okay but may add some cost in tail for small bursts. maybe add a dynamic threshold proportional to current queue depth: wait_ms = min(100, 10 * sqrt(queue_len)).

taylor: could also prioritize KV-prefetch siblings: if one request in batch misses KV and another hits, we can reorder admission to group misses together so prefetcher can warm KV. but that needs accounting for fairness.

maria: logging plan: add compact metrics to batch summary events: {strata_hist, kernel_choice, kv_hit_ratio, batch_token_budget, wait_ms}. keep as single-line JSON in logs to keep parsing cheap.

zane: +1. also add a small offline classifier job to recompute the strata thresholds per route weekly. workloads drift.

perf-bot: note: no alerts fired during canary. flagging a regression ticket if p95 goes above baseline on rollout.

maria: ok will push the longer run results in #eng-runtime tomorrow AM. thanks all :thumbsup:
